items.question: Under what condition does consciousness bear the mark of liberation?
premises: Consciousness can take enjoyment as its nature.
The same consciousness is referred to again in the consequent.
Liberation can be described as a defining mark of consciousness.
items.inference: When consciousness has enjoyment as its nature, that same consciousness is marked by liberation.
uncertainties: The forms cetaṃ and cettam are archaic or non-standard spellings of cetas.
The gender agreement of sa with neuter consciousness forms is irregular and may reflect archaic usage.
items.plain_english: When consciousness is of the nature of enjoyment, that same consciousness bears the mark of liberation.
